newsitem.title: INDIA: ITC tight-lipped on B.A.T deal.
newsitem.headline: ITC tight-lipped on B.A.T deal.

text.p: Indian tobacco and hotels company ITC Ltd said on Monday it would not divulge the details of a licensing agreement with Britain's B.A.T Industries Plc until the Indian government approved the deal.
"We cannot give you any details. We can't even tell you when the agreement was signed," an ITC spokesman in Calcutta told Reuters.
"Probably we can give you the details only after the government's approval," the spokesman said.

Earlier ITC announced the two firms had reached a deal, saying: "B.A.T Industries Plc and ITC Ltd have signed an agreement on licensing of B.A.T brand to ITC, subject to the approval of the government of India," the one-sentence statement said.
India's Business Standard newspaper reported last week that the ITC board had decided to approve a licensing arrangement for the introduction of B.A.T cigarette brands in India.

Quoting unnamed ITC sources, the newspaper said the Indian company would manufacture and market the B.A.T brands under its own portfolio and pay a license fee to B.A.T, which has a 31.7 percent stake in ITC.
